newsitem.title: UK: Taleban order foreigners to Kabul hotel - report.
newsitem.headline: Taleban order foreigners to Kabul hotel - report.

text.p: The fundamentalist Islamic Taleban militia on Friday ordered all foreigners in the Afghan capital Kabul to move to one of the city's hotels, saying they could no longer stay in private accommodation.
A statement from the ministry of civil aviation and tourism, broadcast on pro-Taleban Afghan radio, said the Intercontinental Hotel was "dedicated to foreign guests and ready to serve them".
The broadcast was quoted by BBC Radio.

"The hotel management requests that foreign guests, such as journalists and other foreign nationals staying in ... Rented accommodation, should contact the Intercontinental Hotel," the statement said.
"They are not allowed to stay anywhere else".
The Taleban, which controls Kabul, also said on Friday that it had captured a number of enemy agents in the capital, the British Broadcasting Corporation report said, again citing Kabul radio.

"As a result of efforts by the Intelligence Services Ministry, a number of terrorist and propaganda group leaders, who were deployed by the enemy to disrupt the normal life of our citizens, have been arrested," it quoted Kabul radio as saying.
The Taleban on Friday offered its opponents a mutual pullback of forces from frontlines 20 to 25 kilometres (15 to 19 miles) north of the capital Kabul as part of a U.N.-proposed ceasefire.

Taleban acting foreign minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous said the militia would withdraw to its bases in Kabul if its opponents went back to the Panjsher Valley north of the capital and the northern town of Mazar-i-Sharif.
The Taleban seized Kabul in late September.
